reason: The learner practises merging onto a motorway at seventy miles an hour with her grandmother before passing her test, and the story treats this as fine. Under Highway Code rule 253 (gov.uk), a learner on a GB motorway must be with an approved driving instructor in a dual-control car.

'Even, the review implied, when the positive ones outnumbered them five to one.' The 2001 Baumeister review (citing Gottman) says good interactions must outnumber bad ones by at least five to one for the good to prevail, not that bad still wins at five to one (checked in the review's text).

'He said the tradition calls the broader obligation a fence, a fence around the law.' A 'fence around the Torah' (Pirkei Avot 1:1) means extra rabbinic safeguards against breaking a law. It is not the name for extending the parapet duty to other hazards (Wikipedia, 'Fence around the Torah').

'She had checked the key signature on the score, and there it was, one sharp where there had been none.' In a Mozart C major sonata exposition the key signature does not change. The move to G major is written with accidentals (F sharps), not a new key signature.

'He reversed the two arguments in his assertEquals, ran the test, and watched the bar turn green.' Swapping expected and actual only changes the failure message. assertEquals(14.99, 24.99) fails either way, so the swap cannot make a failing test pass (the girl's test 'Green.' has the same error).

The story places the end of K. 333's second movement development at measure 98 and a retransition around measure 90, with a false recapitulation in the wrong key. That movement is 82 measures long: development mm. 32-50, recapitulation from m. 51 (PTNA piano encyclopedia, enc.piano.or.jp).

uncertain: 'That's the whole judgment, right there, in three volumes.' Thiers's original History ran to ten volumes (Wikipedia). The library copy could be a shorter translated edition, since many editions exist, so this is not failed.

The story has the K. 332 Adagio wander through keys in a development before the recapitulation. That movement is in sonatina form with no development section (Wikipedia, 'Piano Sonata No. 12 (Mozart)'); after the double bar the theme returns at once, turning to B-flat minor.

uncertain: 'One and a half seconds. So it went one and a half times farther than the first one.' This holds only if the horizontal speed was the same as in the first throw, which the story assumes but never states. A flat throw staying up about one second is also generous.
